questions.question: Does the barrier mechanism of the FCC-L12 phase in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 hold when moisture is introduced to the molten salt environment, given that the current study lacks moisture data?
questions.rationale: The paper attributes protection to the FCC-L12 barrier but explicitly notes moisture effects were not evaluated; confirming this boundary is critical for applying the alloy in humid CSP conditions.
questions.decision_use: Determines if the alloy requires additional coating or moisture control strategies before deployment in real-world CSP systems.
answer_requirements: Measure corrosion rates of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in molten salt with controlled moisture additions and compare to anhydrous conditions using weight gain.
evidence_spans: Additionally, the work function increased with increasing temperature for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, indicating that the FCC-L1 2 phase acted as a barrier against further oxidation and protected the underlying BCC-B2 phase
However, a detailed evaluation of the effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior has not been performed in the current study

questions.question: Is the superior corrosion resistance of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in molten chloride primarily due to Al hindering dissolution or micro-galvanic coupling, and can SKP mapping distinguish these mechanisms at 650 °C?
questions.rationale: The paper offers two competing causal explanations (Al hindering vs. micro-galvanic coupling); distinguishing them prevents misdesign of future alloys.
questions.decision_use: Guides whether to prioritize Al content optimization or microstructure control (phase fraction/interface engineering) for next-generation alloys.
answer_requirements: Perform high-resolution SKP mapping at 650 °C to correlate local work function variations with dissolution sites and compare against the hypothesized galvanic coupling model.
evidence_spans: This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy
This may be attributed to the presence of Al in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 that hinders the dissolution of the other alloy constituents in the molten salt

questions.question: At what specific moisture threshold does the FCC-L12 barrier in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 fail, reversing the corrosion advantage over DS2205 seen at 650 °C?
questions.rationale: The alloy shows a massive advantage (9 vs 20 mm/year) now, but the lack of moisture data creates a risk of catastrophic failure in humid environments.
questions.decision_use: Sets the maximum allowable water partial pressure limit for component specifications or dictates the need for drying systems.
answer_requirements: Conduct step-wise corrosion testing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in molten salt with incremental moisture content (0-5 wt%) and identify the point where the rate exceeds 20 mm/year.
evidence_spans: Additionally, the work function increased with increasing temperature for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, indicating that the FCC-L1 2 phase acted as a barrier against further oxidation and protected the underlying BCC-B2 phase
Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205
However, a detailed evaluation of the effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior has not been performed in the current study
